partners.mechanism_chain: DLX5 (HGNC:2716) —LEADS_TO→ Split hand-foot malformation (HP:0001718); DLX5 (HGNC:2716) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405); PSMC3 (HGNC:9786) —DISRUPTS→ 26S proteasome complex assembly (GO:0000410); 26S proteasome complex assembly (GO:0000410) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental disorder (HP:0001263). DLX5 is a transcription factor crucial for limb and inner ear development. Haploinsufficiency of DLX5 leads to split hand-foot malformations and sensorineural hearing loss. PSMC3 is a subunit of the 26S proteasome, essential for protein degradation. Loss-of-function mutations in PSMC3 impair proteasome function, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular stress, which underlies the neurodevelopmental defects seen in Ebstein-Bezieau syndrome. The convergence lies in the disruption of critical cellular machinery for development and homeostasis, with DLX5 acting as a transcriptional regulator and PSMC3 as a component of a major protein degradation complex, both essential for proper cellular function and organismal development.
